method: Capacity: the aggregate demand is the peak device count times the target throughput per device in Mbps; the usable throughput of one access point is its throughput after the headroom percentage is held back; the number of access points for capacity is the demand divided by that usable throughput, rounded up. Coverage: the floor area in square metres divided by the coverage area of one access point, rounded up. The plan takes the larger of the two counts, so a capacity-limited plan runs at 100% minus the headroom in airtime when every client asks for its full target, and a coverage-limited plan carries less load per access point. Inputs: floor area 1 to 100000 m2, devices a whole number from 1 to 100000, target throughput 0.1 to 10000 Mbps, usable throughput per AP 1 to 10000 Mbps, coverage area per AP 1 to 20000 m2, and headroom 0 to 50 percent. Throughput values are rounded half up to one decimal, counts are exact integers, and a plan never drops below one access point. The model is a first-pass budget: it assumes uniform device demand and a uniform coverage cell, and it does not model walls, ceilings, antenna patterns, the band or channel width, spatial streams, interference, roaming overlap, client capability or a site survey, so measured throughput can differ. Everything is calculated in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN capacity planning: aggregate offered load divided by usable per-access-point throughput

Wi-Fi airtime efficiency: usable application throughput is roughly 40 to 60 percent of the PHY rate after contention, management traffic and retries
